transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-05 14:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Recorded: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Riley Nguyen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Kapoor (Zenith Head of AI), Marcus Li (Infra), Sara Gomez (Security), Luis Ortega (App)

Summary: discovery focused on on-prem / air-gapped deployment options for regulated PHI workloads. Key topics: hardware constraints, offline update process, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and RBAC, timeline and pilot scope.

Topics:
- Why Zenith is evaluating private on-prem: PHI/data residency + regulatory audits
- Air-gapped update workflow and approvals
- Hardware inventory, GPUs, and performance expectations
- Security controls: SSO, SAML, HSM, audit logs, retention
- Next steps and pilot scope

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to chat through your on-prem needs - uh do a quick intros - i can kick off then ethan will lead the technical section.
[00:15] Dr. Priya: hi thanks, excited - we run patient triage and clinical summarization models, pretty sensitive PHI, so primary req is no data leaves the VPC and ideally air-gapped updates.
[00:30] Marcus: yeah also limited maintenance windows - 2 hours monthly for updates, and we have about 16 GPU hosts across two data centers.
[00:45] Ethan (SE): okay good, that helps, and when you say air-gapped updates - do you mean physically disconnected environments or logically restricted?
[01:00] Sara (Security): we mean physically disconnected, network egress blocked by policy, only approved media and signed artifacts allowed. we need to be able to attest to update provenance.
[01:15] Riley (SE): got it - Redwood Private supports on-prem air-gapped installs; artifacts can be exported as signed bundles and pulled into your update pipeline. we do have customers that use removable media or an internal artifact mirror.
[01:30] Luis (App): couple of quicks - latency targets for real-time triage are 200ms p95 for single-turn inference, and throughput for batch summarization is about 20 req/s, so cost/latency trade off matters.
[01:45] Ethan: ok, that's helpful. for 200ms p95 on 16 hosts, we want to understand model architecture and KV cache behavior - small note, a lot of transcription engines call KV cache K-V cash, but i mean key-value cache.
[02:00] Dr. Priya: we plan to use a 7B quantized model for most workloads, occasionally 13B for complex notes.
[02:15] Maya: quick qual - what's your timeline for a pilot?
[02:30] Marcus: 1 quarter to get a pilot running and another for production signoff, need everything in place before jan 2026.
[02:45] Maya: great. Ethan can you walk through the on-prem deployment steps, like how the control plane works with air-gapped nodes?
[03:00] Ethan: sure - high level: Redwood Private offers a customer-managed control plane that can operate behind your network. in air-gapped mode we support a small, local control plane or an offline mode where the control plane is internal and updates happen via signed bundles. the control plane does not phone home for normal inference, only for telemetry or optional features; all of that can be disabled.
[03:20] Marcus: so no outbound to redwood by default?
[03:25] Ethan: correct, you can fully disable outbound. there is an offline update flow: we provide an update artifact signed with our PKI, you verify signature and then install via your ops process. some customers mirror artifacts to an internal registry.
[03:40] Sara: what's the story on KMS/HSM? we use an on-prem HSM from Thales currently.
[03:45] Riley: we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping and signing. you can bring your own keys and keep them in your HSM; Redwood will not store unwrapped keys. in some installs we ship an operator that interacts with the HSM via PKCS#11.
[04:10] Dr. Priya: audit logs - we need immutable audit trails for inference requests tied to user identities for compliance.
[04:20] Ethan: we emit structured audit logs that can be exported to your SIEM. logs are configurable for retention, and we can integrate with your logging stack. note that in air-gapped mode we write to local object storage and you push to your SIEM on your schedule.
[04:35] Luis: how granular is RBAC? we have app teams and clinical reviewers with different privileges.
[04:40] Maya: we support role based access plus SAML/SSO, can map groups to roles and have per-route policies.
[04:50] Marcus: any compliance certifications we should know about? SOC2, ISO?
[04:55] Maya: yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II and is working toward ISO but we will send the latest security pack. for the on-prem package we include a runbook, architecture diagrams, and audit artifacts.
[05:10] Sara: nice, we'll need the SOC2 and a statement of how you handle repo signing and build pipeline.
[05:20] Maya: will do - i'll include CI/CD signing details in the packet.
[05:25] Ethan: on performance - given your 7B quantized model target, with 16 A100 equals or equivalent, we can likely meet the 200ms p95 for single-turn if we use low-latency scheduling and keep KV caches warm. but if you have conservative eviction windows or cold starts, there's a hit.
[05:45] Dr. Priya: what about batching - can we do batching for summarization jobs without impacting triage latency?
[05:55] Ethan: yes, we support workload-aware routing: low-latency route for triage pinned to dedicated pool, and batch route for summarization on a different pool, or we can use dynamic pool scaling in Dedicated. in private we recommend isolating critical routes.
[06:15] Marcus: hardware note - our hosts are older V100s for some racks and a few newer A40s. will that be a problem?
[06:25] Ethan: V100s are still usable for certain quantized models, but you will see higher latency compared to A100/A40. we will provide model profiles and kernel selection guidance. also quantization strategy matters.
[06:40] Riley: also important - if you plan to mix hardware, we recommend model variants per hardware class and a routing policy. Redwood's runtime can auto-fallback to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained. that helps during upgrade windows.
[06:55] Luis: how do offline updates work for model weights? do we need to recompile or is it a drop-in?
[07:05] Ethan: model artifact is a signed bundle with weights and metadata; the runtime will load compatible variants. sometimes we run a lightweight optimization/compilation step on the host for kernel selection - that can be part of the update window. we can precompile for your hardware and ship those artifacts to save time.
[07:30] Dr. Priya: that precompilation option sounds critical since our maintenance window is tight.
[07:40] Maya: noted - we'll include an option for precompiled kernels in the runbook.
[07:50] Sara: regarding attestations, we need cryptographic proof of the update artifact origin and a chain of custody for install. is that possible?
[07:58] Riley: yes, artifacts signed by Redwood's key and optionally re-signed by your operational signing key; we can produce install receipts and attestations tied to your KMS.
[08:10] Marcus: what about telemetry and metrics? we want internal observability but not external.
[08:15] Ethan: all telemetry can be kept local; we push metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana. optional usage reporting can be turned off.
[08:25] Luis: any limitations around model size when running in air-gapped? like multi-GPU shards?
[08:35] Ethan: multi-GPU sharding works but needs network fabric considerations; in air-gapped you still have an internal network so that works if your fabric supports RDMA. otherwise you may prefer model parallelism that fits single host. we'll need to look at your network.
[08:55] Dr. Priya: can we run evaluations / rouge/bleu regression tests locally with Redwood's eval harness?
[09:05] Riley: yes, we can provide the eval harness and you can run locally. we also support offline collection of eval metrics and alerts for regressions.
[09:15] Maya: quick qual on stakeholders - who owns sign-off on security and procurement?
[09:20] Sara: security sign-off is me, procurement is with legal but Marcus will run the infra validation.
[09:30] Maya: ok, next steps we typically do: send security pack + on-prem runbook, SE to do hardware sizing and schedule deep dive. any other asks?
[09:40] Marcus: sample dataset - i'll upload a sanitized sample for benchmarking.
[09:45] Luis: also please include pricing for a 3-month pilot and an expansion scenario to 32 hosts.
[09:55] Maya: will do.
[10:00] Dr. Priya: one more, SLA expectations for private on-prem?
[10:05] Maya: on-prem does not include hosted SLAs by default, but we offer an enterprise support add-on with runbook guaranteed response times and optional on-site assistance. will include options.
[10:20] Ethan: quick technical note - for the 200ms p95 you will want low-latency pinning and warm KV caches; also consider small token limits for triage route to bound compute.
[10:35] Riley: and for your air-gapped update cadence, consider a staging cluster where you apply the signed bundle first, run smoke tests, then promote to prod - that reduces risk.
[10:50] Maya: thanks all, i'll send the packet tomorrow and ethan will prepare the sizing doc. let's tentatively schedule the SE deep dive for 2025-10-09?
[10:58] Marcus: 2025-10-09 works for infra deep dive.
[11:05] Maya: great. thanks everyone.
